route: Explicit code labels in the paper (Step 5b exemption) + route 9 response-frequency matching against the study's own raw CSV
evidence: S1 Appendix Table A1 labels each item with the code the data uses (ARP1/ARP2/ARP3), and the S3 CSV's columns carry the same three names. Per-item resp counts for levels 1..7 match the raw column cell for cell: ARP1 21/9/20/56/69/58/112 raw vs 21/9/20/56/69/58/112 live; ARP2 10/6/21/50/56/66/136 vs 10/6/21/50/56/66/136; ARP3 7/7/14/46/66/62/143 vs 7/7/14/46/66/62/143. The three count vectors are pairwise distinct, so the match discriminates the items rather than being satisfied by any permutation. Does NOT establish: that the authors' own appendix table is correctly labelled (an error inside Table A1 is undetectable here), and says nothing about option_text -- no anchors are published, so option_text ships blank and is unverified.

Paper Table 2 means 4.661 / 5.191 / 4.901 for CFS1 / CFS2 / CFS3 reproduce exactly (diff <0.0005) from the live table for codes CFS1 / CFS3 / CFS4 respectively (n=345 each). The three means are mutually distinct with a minimum gap of 0.240, so no other permutation of the three texts fits; every item is distinguished from every other. Does NOT establish the response anchors (paper says only '7-point Likert scale' and publishes no labels, so option_text ships blank for resp 1-7), and does not establish the administration language. Table 2's St. Dev. column was not usable - it gives 1.304/1.331/1.318 against observed raw SDs of 1.873/1.752/1.891 and repeats 1.611 for two different ARP items.

route: explicit code labels in the paper (Step 5b exemption) + 9 (per-item response-frequency matching, source column vs live code)
evidence: Two-link chain, both links checked. Link 1 (label match, no inference): S1 Appendix Table A1 prints the codes SNO1, SNO2, SNO3 beside their wording, and the S1 File CSV header carries exactly those three names -- the Step 5b 'explicit code labels in the paper' exemption, with 3/3 codes matching verbatim. Link 2 (checked numerically, verify_jo_2023_sno.R): per-item counts at scale points 1-7 match the raw S1 column cell for cell, 0 of 21 cells differing -- SNO1 5/2/6/48/57/79/148 raw vs 5/2/6/48/57/79/148 live (mean 5.8377 vs 5.8377), SNO2 1/1/6/30/57/70/180 vs identical (6.1043), SNO3 1/1/5/29/59/69/181 vs identical (6.1159), n=345 each. The three columns are mutually distinguishable, so this rules out every permutation and not just gross ones: the near-tied SNO2/SNO3 (means 6.1043 vs 6.1159) are separated by their level counts, and each of the five rival mappings misses on 10, 10, 14, 17 and 17 of 21 cells. NOT established by this route: the option_text<->resp axis, which is untested because the study published no anchor labels and option_text ships blank for all 7 levels; and the administered language, which the authors never state -- the language='Korean; Vietnamese' value the extraction proposed was reverted by the orchestrator at Step 5b as unsupported (the deposit's Hangul occurs only in the free-text 'Software' column).
